claims.text: An active-learning-driven MLIP can accurately compute solid and fluid free energies across the fusion transition in complex high-temperature materials.
On-the-fly corrections can retain electron–vibration coupling and anharmonic contributions in the MLIP free-energy workflow.
The proposed workflow will cost 5–10 times less than explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed workflow will maintain approximately 5% fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
Vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration effects are significant near melting in the targeted elemental, binary, and multicomponent systems.
The MLIP will be trained by active learning on configurations sampled within ±50 K of the melting point using short ab initio molecular-dynamics trajectories.
Sampling regions of high prediction uncertainty near phase boundaries will rapidly refine the MLIP.
Active refinement near phase boundaries will incorporate the critical anharmonic interactions.
Active refinement near phase boundaries will incorporate the critical electron–vibration interactions.
The corrected MLIP will enable metadynamics or thermodynamic integration to calculate phase free energies more efficiently than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
MLIP phase free energies will match explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics evaluations.
The method will predict melting temperatures with fidelity comparable to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The method will predict latent heats with fidelity comparable to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The method will reduce computational expense by roughly one order of magnitude.
The method will scale better than TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The proposed applicability extends from pure elements and binary alloys to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed temperature domain is within ±50 K of the melting point.
